artifacts.summary: Diagnoses test-guard-git-push.sh's expired-grant failure as an ambient env var leak (PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW=1800 exported by ~/.claude/settings.json widens pg_grant_fresh()'s window past the test's hardcoded 700s offset), not a grant-matching/test-isolation defect; recommends a one-line 'unset PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW' fixture fix.

claim_invalidations.claim: test-guard-git-push.sh's expired-grant case failure is NOT ambient-host-state coupling and is instead a grant-matching/test-isolation defect in push-grant-lib.sh or guard-git-push.sh, as stated in specs/170_isolate_shell_suites_from_host_state/reports/02_corpus-triage-ledger.md and known-failures.txt row 40.

memory_candidates.content: A shell-test fixture that asserts a relative-time 'expired' threshold against a library constant must isolate EVERY environment-overridable knob the library reads via ${VAR:-default}, not just the file-path/key-path-shaped ones that look state-bearing. push-grant-lib.sh's PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW (default 600s) is deliberately overridable so the guard hook and the /please wrapper agree on one session-wide value; this machine's ~/.claude/settings.json env block sets it to 1800 for every session. test-guard-git-push.sh isolated PUSH_GRANT_DIR and PUSH_GRANT_KEY_PATH but omitted PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW, so its hardcoded 700s-old 'expired' fixture (valid against the 600s default) silently passed under the real 1800s ambient value. Fix: unset/pin every env-overridable constant a fixture's pass/fail boundary depends on, found by grepping the library for ${VAR:-default} patterns, not just by isolating paths.

A single env -u <VAR> toggle on an otherwise-unmodified failing test command is a fast, decisive way to confirm/rule out an ambient-environment-variable cause before adding tracing to production code: if unsetting flips the result cleanly (e.g. 46/1 failed -> 47/0 passed) with no other change, the env var is both necessary and sufficient, and no deeper instrumentation of the library under test is warranted.
